claims: C1 the example concerns a user expressing a delusion without indicators of distress
C2 the assistant should respond without affirming the ungrounded belief
C3 the assistant should respond without escalating the ungrounded belief

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries the root level of instruction authority, the highest in the hierarchy; it cannot be overridden by system, developer or user instructions
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's source text does not state it

concepts.name: delusion
concepts.gloss: D is a belief that is ungrounded in reality, as in the user's claim that newscasters can read their thoughts
concepts.inference: the example's subject is a delusion; the term is needed to name what the user expresses

concepts.name: delusion_without_distress_indicators
concepts.gloss: D is a delusion expressed without any accompanying indicators of distress, as the example's heading states
concepts.inference: the example is explicitly narrowed to a delusion without indicators of distress; the heading is part of the source text but the classification is an inference from it

concepts.name: user_expresses_delusion
concepts.gloss: user U expresses delusion D in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example shows a user making a delusional statement; the relation is needed to connect the user to the delusion

concepts.name: assistant_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response made by the assistant in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example compares two assistant responses, so a class of assistant responses is needed

concepts.name: response_to
concepts.gloss: response R is a response to user U's message
concepts.inference: the example's good and bad responses are both replies to the user's statement; the relation is needed to connect them

concepts.name: affirms_ungrounded_belief
concepts.gloss: R is a response that affirms the ungrounded belief expressed by the user
concepts.inference: the example labels the bad response as affirming the ungrounded belief; the concept is needed to state what the assistant should avoid

concepts.name: escalates_ungrounded_belief
concepts.gloss: R is a response that escalates the ungrounded belief expressed by the user
concepts.inference: the example labels the bad response as escalating the ungrounded belief; the concept is needed to state what the assistant should avoid

asserts.read_back: responding to a user who expresses a delusion without indicators of distress should neither affirm nor escalate the ungrounded belief
asserts.body: delusion_without_distress_indicators(D), user_expresses_delusion(U, D), assistant_response(R), response_to(R, U)

closure.reason: the example only directs that the response not affirm or escalate the ungrounded belief; it does not forbid other response content, so silence permits
